title: The Forearm That Shook the Room
synopsis: A young man arrives calm but crashing — a dog bite to his right forearm three hours ago has already lit a systemic fire. The monitor tells the story before the wound does: 87% oxygen, lactate 4.5, a body losing perfusion while the patient still tries to smile.

chapters.heading: Arrival
chapters.body: He walks in, but barely — a young Black man in a patterned shirt, his right forearm wrapped in a blood-stained towel. The triage nurse clocks the SpO₂ first: 87% on room air. His respiratory rate is 24, shallow and fast, and his skin is warm despite the hypotension. He says the dog was a neighbor's, a big one, and the bite happened three hours ago. He thought he could wait it out.
chapters.visualHint: ED bay — patient sitting on gurney edge, right forearm wrapped in towel, bare feet dangling over mattress edge. Monitor shows HR 116, BP 82/50, SpO₂ 87%. His face is calm but his breathing is visibly rapid.

chapters.heading: The Monitor First
chapters.body: The attending doesn't unwrap the arm yet — she reads the numbers. Lactate 4.5. Heart rate 116. Blood pressure 82/50. The bite is on the forearm, but the body is already in a fight: catecholamines from pain and fear, cytokines from deep inoculation. His tachypnea isn't lung disease — it's the systemic inflammatory response stealing his reserve. She orders oxygen by mask and two large-bore IVs before she even looks at the wound.
chapters.visualHint: Attending at monitor, hand on nasal cannula being placed. Patient's right arm still wrapped, IV start kit on bedside table. His toes curl against the mattress as the nurse palpates for a vein.

chapters.heading: The Wound
chapters.body: The towel comes off. The right forearm shows two puncture wounds, deep and already surrounded by spreading erythema — the skin is hot, tight, and tender to the edge of the cellulitis. This is not a simple laceration; the dog's mouth drove oral flora deep into the tissue planes. The crush component means devitalized tissue underneath, a perfect culture medium. The attending calls for irrigation, debridement, and wound cultures — but only after the first liter of fluid is running.
chapters.visualHint: Close-up over attending's shoulder — right forearm exposed, two dark puncture wounds with red streaking extending toward the elbow. Gloved hand holding saline syringe. IV tubing running into left antecubital.

chapters.heading: The Systemic Fire
chapters.body: The first liter of normal saline brings the blood pressure to 94/60, but the heart rate stays at 110 and the lactate hasn't budged. The attending knows: fluids buy time, but source control is the lever. She orders the wound debridement now, while the patient is still awake and perfusing. The ID consult is paged for rabies PEP and antibiotic coverage — the timeline matters, but the sepsis comes first. The patient's eyes are still open, but his answers are slower now.
chapters.visualHint: Patient supine now, oxygen mask on, right arm being prepped with betadine by a gloved team. Second IV bag hanging. His gaze is fixed on the ceiling, toes still visible at frame bottom.

chapters.heading: The Margin
chapters.body: He is wheeled to the procedure room for debridement. The airway is patent — the bite is on the forearm, not the face — but the attending knows that exhaustion and hypoxemia can steal reserve silently. The oxygen is still running, the fluids are still dripping, and the lactate is the clock. The dog is quarantined for observation. The rabies vaccine series will start tonight. For now, the room is quiet except for the pulse oximeter — 94% now, climbing.
chapters.visualHint: Gurney moving through hallway, patient's right arm elevated on pillow with dressing, oxygen tank rolling alongside. His bare feet at frame edge. Overhead fluorescent lights pass in streaks.

patientLock: Young adult Black male, patterned hospital gown, calm but ill expression — likeness consistent across all images: medium build, short natural hair, no facial hair, right forearm injury visible or dressed.
